analysis_steps.goal: Construct cluster lens models, identify multiple images, and compute magnifications and UV-FIR offset

method.value: Build three independent cluster mass models using GLAFIC, LENSTOOL, and Light-Traces-Mass (LTM) constrained by 9 other secure multiply-imaged systems (5 with MUSE redshifts) to predict multiple image positions and magnification factors, and measure UV-to-FIR spatial offset.

evidence.quote: The three models used here are produced using GLAFIC (cite: GLAFIC), LENSTOOL (cite: Lenstool), and Light-Traces-Mass (LTM; (cite: Zitrin2015)).
Four modellers (MO, JR, GC, AZ) voted on the choice of multiply-imaged systems which, besides the $z\sim6$ system, included nine other systems considered as secure.
We also take benefit from the detection of the dust continuum in two of the multiple images (z6.3 and the arc) to estimate the physical offset between the FIR continuum and the UV continuum.

key_parameters.value: Three to four dark matter halos for parametric models

evidence.quote: The parametric modeling of MACS0600 typically included three to four dark matter halos and, whereas for the LTM models, the masses of several bright cluster members were modeled independently.

assumptions.value: Pseudo isothermal elliptical mass distributions and empirical scaling relations for parametric models; dark matter follows smoothed luminosity-weighted galaxy distribution for LTM

evidence.quote: The first two models can be regarded as parametric, in the sense that both the galaxies and their dark matter halos are described using independent analytic forms (e.g., combinations of pseudo isothermal elliptical mass distributions) and adopt empirical scaling relations for cluster members.
The LTM method is similar, but here the dark matter is assumed to follow the light distribution and thus is modeled as a smoothed version of the luminosity-weighted galaxy distribution.

fitting.value: Minimization using multiple image constraints; source position adjusted in LENSTOOL/GLAFIC to match [CII] 158 um line flux ratio; arc delensed in LTM

evidence.quote: All models are minimized using available multiple image constraints to find the best-fit solution and its associated errors.

The two parametric models (LENSTOOL and GLAFIC) extracted values by first planting a compact source in the expected position, and adjusting its exact position with respect to the critical curves to match the observed \[CII\] 158 $\mu$m line flux ratio.

validation.value: Checked consistency of WFC3 colors (F125W-F160W = 0.32 +/- 0.15), F160W surface brightness (21.9 +/- 0.3), 1.2 mm continuum flux ratio, and [C II] 158 um detections across multiple images.

evidence.quote: Colors measured on WFC3 images are similar with averaged values of F125W-F160W = 0.32$\pm$0.15.

why_this_data.value: Strong gravitational lensing by the foreground cluster MACSJ0600.1-2008 observed in the ALMA Lensing Cluster Survey provides the high magnification (mu >= 30) needed to probe dust and physical properties in an intrinsically faint, sub-luminous galaxy at z >= 6.

evidence.quote: We use a detailed mass model of the cluster and infer a magnification $\mu\gtrsim$30 for the most magnified image of this galaxy, which provides an unprecedented opportunity to probe the physical properties of a sub-luminous galaxy at the end of cosmic reionisation.

With current facilities, the only way to characterise the physical properties of this sub-luminous population is to use the magnification afforded by gravitational lensing (for a review see (cite: Kneib2011)).

why_this_method.value: A 2'' uv-taper was applied to ALMA data to maximise detection of faint sources; GALFIT Sersic modelling was used to deblend overlapping foreground and lensed sources and account for PSF differences; three independent lens models were used to assess magnification and positional uncertainties.

evidence.quote: A 2$''$ *uv*-taper was used to maximise the detection of faint sources.

Noting the overlapping foreground object, in order to extract the photometry of MACS0600-arc we model each source with a Sersic profile using GALFIT (cite: GALFIT) on the WFC3-NIR and IRAC images, which accounts for PSF difference between HST, VLT and Spitzer.
To determine the lensing configuration and hence the intrinsic properties of this source and the associated uncertainties, we have utilised several different lens models from within the ALCS team.
